A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same broadcast-product formalism and broadcast decomposition. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 Section VII-C and Figure 2 report original synthetic-tensor reconstruction experiments comparing broadcast decomposition with CPD, Tucker, and tensor-ring decomposition.

after.justification: v2 Section 5.3 and Figure 5 report synthetic reconstruction results and an additional experiment using real traffic-speed data.

M1.justification: The broadcast operator, BD and summed-BD models, least-squares objective, and ALS/HALS updates are retained from v1 Section VII in v2 Section 5. The explicit shape conventions and initialization cautions clarify the existing procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only a synthetic 32-by-32-by-32 tensor. v2 adds a real traffic-speed tensor of shape 32-by-21-by-24, substantially extending coverage beyond data generated by BD itself. The added normalization and blending examples are algebraic illustrations, not evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain canonical polyadic decomposition, Tucker decomposition, and tensor-ring decomposition. v2 extends this same comparator set to traffic data; the additional related-work discussions do not introduce experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new traffic experiment treats the original tensor as ground truth, adds Gaussian noise, and evaluates reconstruction SNR across model sizes. No revision to the existing synthetic evaluation protocol is stated. The explicit SNR formula primarily documents the previously used metric.

E4.justification: Neither version reports separate ablations, initialization-sensitivity tests, controlled robustness studies, or error analyses. v2 extends the reconstruction-versus-parameter comparison to traffic data without adding such an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental repetition counts or random seeds, or reports confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. Both versions present performance curves without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 5(b) adds substantive real-data findings: BD generally lies between CPD/TRD and Tucker over much of the parameter range. Several synthetic BD values also change, including approximately 44.4 to 45.4 dB near 27,600 parameters, while the baseline curves and synthetic ranking persist. These are revised reported values, with no documented explanation for the revision.

T1.justification: v2 adds the Cauchy-Schwarz norm bound and its proof in Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A, broadcast-operator identities in Appendix C, and formal tensor-network and Khatri-Rao relationships. The existing least-squares derivation is retained as Appendix D, rather than being a new proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain broadcast notation and a decomposition built from it. v2 explicitly prioritizes notation and mathematical formalization, labels BD a preliminary, noncentral proof of concept, and disclaims empirical superiority. This qualifies the contribution without replacing its core.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that BD-generated synthetic data favor BD by construction, treats traffic results as preliminary, and discusses zero-denominator failures and unresolved initialization sensitivity. It also adds substantive guidance on when broadcast notation, explicit shape annotation, or Named Tensor Notation is preferable.

D1.justification: v2 supplies demonstration-code and traffic-data links, clarifies the SNR ground-truth target, adds Julia broadcasting examples, and provides operator-entry instructions in Appendix F. Experimental noise magnitudes, solver budgets, and repetition details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The brief related-work discussion becomes a substantive comparison with existing tensor products and notation systems, especially Named Tensor Notation in Section 6.3. New references cover tensor-network diagrams, normalization methods, einx, and TensorLy, materially expanding research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract and introduction, adds an explicit contribution list and conclusion, reorganizes operator properties and examples, and expands related work into thematic subsections. The appendices are reorganized, and the NumPy explanation is rewritten with parallel Julia examples.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, adds tensor-network diagrams in Figures 2-4 and 7, expands the performance figure into synthetic/traffic panels, and adds the operator-input Table 2. Existing diagrams and the symbol-conflict table are retained with relocation or redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the mathematical exposition and positioning through explicit shape conventions, a proved norm bound, unified normalization examples, and comparison with Named Tensor Notation. Construction-bias caveats and mixed traffic results also make the empirical interpretation better calibrated than v1's synthetic-only demonstration. These gains outweigh the localized fold/unfold inconsistency in Eq. (49), although experimental settings and uncertainty reporting remain incomplete.
